speaker_role: independent counselor/consultancy marketer (founder of 'Next Admit' college admissions consulting)
commercial_incentive: Promotes his own consulting service, essay review service, and upcoming 'college essay boot camp' throughout the video
key_insights: Recommends building a college list of about 6-12 schools split into roughly 3 safeties, 4-5 matches, 2-3 reaches, defining tiers by where your GPA/test scores fall relative to a school's middle 50th/75th/25th percentiles

Notes Ivy League and top-20 schools are reaches for everyone regardless of stats, since academic credentials are only a threshold there -- extracurriculars, essays, and letters differentiate applicants
Describes 'shotgunning' (applying to nearly every Ivy/top-20 school) as a recognized trend, motivated by both prestige-chasing and strong financial aid at elite schools

Lists college-list factors to weigh: size, class size/student-faculty ratio, urban vs rural location, distance from home, climate, available majors/curriculum flexibility, campus culture/traditions, residential life, extracurricular breadth, and cost via net price calculators
Explains early action/early decision/restrictive early action distinctions and recommends finishing SAT/ACT testing by summer before senior year if applying early
Recommends creating a separate email address for all college admissions communications and drafting essays in a separate Google Doc before copying into the Common App
Advises asking only junior-year (or at most sophomore) teachers for recommendation letters, in person, and providing them a 'brag sheet' of accomplishments
Notes typical application costs $50-80 each, and recommends checking Common App fee waiver eligibility

Outlines post-submission steps: mid-year grade reports still matter, interviews are casual conversations (common at many top-20 schools), and financial aid appeal letters are a legitimate option if an award is insufficient
specific_numbers_or_facts: Recommends about 6-12 total schools split 3 safety / 4-5 match / 2-3 reach
Says the average college application costs $50-80
States early application deadlines are usually around November 1 and regular deadlines around January 1
States National College Decision Day is May 1
Says three letters of recommendation are typically required: one counselor, two teachers
notable_or_distinctive: Provides an unusually complete step-by-step operational walkthrough of the entire application timeline (list-building through decision day) in one video, including concrete tactical advice like using a separate email address and drafting essays outside the Common App portal.
reliability_notes: Presented by a for-profit admissions consultant with repeated promotion of his paid essay review and boot camp services; substantive procedural advice appears generally consistent with standard guidance, but figures like application costs and deadlines are generalizations that vary by school.
